title: Tensor closure of the rational localizing categories
statement:
Work in the standing scheme setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], with $X$ a scheme in that setting. Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite subextension of the fixed $\Qlb$. Let $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, using the condensed rings of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], respectively. In particular the latter uses continuous sections with image in a single finite subextension. The notation $\Loc(\Dbc(X,\Lambda))$ means the smallest full replete triangulated subcategory of the ambient unbounded derived category $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ containing $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ and closed under its small coproducts, as in [det-def-localizing-closure-existence].

1. $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ is closed under $\otimes^{\mathbf L}$ in
   $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$.
2. For $A,B\in\Loc(\Dbc(X,\Lambda))$, the derived tensor product
   $A\otimes^{\mathbf L}B$, formed in $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$, lies in
   $\Loc(\Dbc(X,\Lambda))$.

proof.text: For each canonical finite coefficient field E and for the finite-subextension-valued algebraic closure, clause (4) of [sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit] identifies the constant-model bounded constructible predicate with boundedConstructible. Apply the already stated and proved boundedConstructible_tensor_closure of [lem-sfb-dc-tensor-preserves]. Its characteristic hypothesis follows from ringChar k = p and p != ell. This proves clause (1) for the canonical coefficient rings without repeating the locally closed generator argument.

Let phi be the inverse of the monoid-object isomorphism in hLambda. Restriction along phi_X is an exact equivalence by [def-sfb-modobj-restriction-equivalence]. Reuse the proved generic constantModel_comap_iff and constructible_iso helpers in the module of [lem-sfb-integral-constant-model-heart-closure]; these helpers have no integral coefficient hypotheses. They transport finite presentations and finite constant models across the ring isomorphism, commuting restriction with scheme pullback [def-sfb-comap-upper-star-iso]. On derived categories the exact equivalence preserves and reflects boundedness and commutes with homology, hence preserves and reflects constant-model bounded constructibility [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. The derived monoidal comparison tensorLeftCompMapDerivedCategoryIso identifies restriction of a tensor with the tensor of the restricted factors. Isomorphism invariance follows directly from boundedness and the homology functors, using constructible_iso. The generic transport helper accepts the tensor wrappers together with explicit equalities to the canonical curried tensor, so it does not unfold the concrete monoidal constructions. This now transports the tensor closure of step 1 to Lambda. This proves clause (1) with the original monoid-object coefficient hypothesis.

proof.text: An inverse image of a localizing object property P under an exact left adjoint F is localizing. The triangulated inverse-image instance supplies its triangulated closure. For a diagram G valued in the inverse image, P contains colim(G composed with F); the colimit comparison isomorphism identifies this with F(colim G), proving coproduct closure. Derived tensor in each variable is exact by the existing Shift module [lem-sc-source-kflat-tensor-left-triangulated], and is a left adjoint by closedness and braiding [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Thus this observation applies to tensoring on either side. The private equality derivedTensor_eq_curriedTensor identifies the public wrapper with the canonical curried tensor bifunctor. The generic bifunctor closure lemma accepts this equality explicitly, avoiding repeated instance conversions and using precisely the same tensor product.

source.place: Proof (1) exactness and proof (2) coproduct preservation; implemented by localizing_inverseImage using the Mathlib triangulated inverse-image instance and preservesColimitIso

proof.text: Put S = Dbc(X,Lambda) and L = localizingClosure S. By [det-def-localizing-closure-existence], L is localizing and contains S. For B in S, the inverse image of L under tensorRight B is localizing by step 3 and contains S by clause (1). The defining minimality of localizingClosure therefore gives L(A tensor B) for every A in L.

For A in L, the inverse image of L under tensorLeft A is localizing by step 3 and contains S by step 4. Minimality again gives L(A tensor B) for every B in L. This proves clause (2) using the same ambient derived tensor and localizing closure as in the statement.

proof_origin.place: Proof (2), both localizing minimality arguments retained; shorter proof of (1) via the existing coefficient comparison and bounded-constructible tensor closure, with explicit coefficient-isomorphism transport (2026-10-20).
